sanskrit: abhyetya rājānam amitrahābravīj; jayo 'stu te pārthiva bhadram astu ca hayeṣu yukto nṛpa saṃmataḥ sadā; tavāśvasūto nipuṇo bhavāmy aham
english: Approaching the king, the slayer of enemies said: 'Victory to you, O lord of the earth, and may all blessings be yours. Yoked to horses, O king, I am always skilled; I shall be your expert groom.'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca dadāmi yānāni dhanaṃ niveśanaṃ; mamāśvasūto bhavituṃ tvam arhasi kuto 'si kasyāsi kathaṃ tvam āgataḥ; prabrūhi śilpaṃ tava vidyate ca yat
english: Virata said: 'I give you carriages, wealth, and a dwelling — you are worthy to be my horse-keeper. But where are you from? Whose are you? How did you come here? Tell me fully the skill that you possess.'

sanskrit: nakula uvāca pañcānāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ jyeṣṭho rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tenāham aśveṣu purā prakṛtaḥ śatrukarśana
english: Nakula said: 'Among the five sons of Pandu, the eldest king is Yudhishthira. By him I was formerly appointed over horses, O afflicator of enemies.'

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ prakṛtiṃ vedmi vinayaṃ cāpi sarvaśaḥ duṣṭānāṃ pratipattiṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ caiva cikitsitam
english: 'I know the nature of horses and their training in every respect, the handling of vicious ones, and the complete treatment of their ailments.'

sanskrit: na kātaraṃ syān mama jātu vāhanaṃ; na me 'sti duṣṭā vaḍavā kuto hayāḥ janas tu mām āha sa cāpi pāṇḍavo; yudhiṣṭhiro granthikam eva nāmataḥ
english: 'No mount would ever be timid under me; I have no unruly mares — much less stallions. The people call me Granthika, and so too does that Pandava Yudhishthira.'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca yad asti kiṃ cin mama vājivāhanaṃ; tad astu sarvaṃ tvadadhīnam adya vai ye cāpi ke cin mama vājiyojakās; tvadāśrayāḥ sārathayaś ca santu me
english: Virata said: 'Whatever horse-conveyances I possess, let all of them be under your authority from this day forward. And whatever horse-trainers and charioteers I have, let them be under your command.'

sanskrit: idaṃ taveṣṭaṃ yadi vai suropama; bravīhi yat te prasamīkṣitaṃ vasu na te 'nurūpaṃ hayakarma vidyate; prabhāsi rājeva hi saṃmato mama
english: 'If this pleases you, O god-like one, tell me whatever wealth you desire. The work of a groom seems unworthy of you — you shine like a king in my estimation.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasyeva hi darśanena me; samaṃ tavedaṃ priyadarśa darśanam kathaṃ tu bhṛtyaiḥ sa vinākṛto vane; vasaty anindyo ramate ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: 'Indeed, your appearance equals that of Yudhishthira himself in my sight, O fair one. But how is it that the blameless Pandava, separated from his servants, dwells in the forest and finds his pleasure there?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā sa gandharvavaropamo yuvā; virāṭarājñā muditena pūjitaḥ na cainam anye 'pi viduḥ kathaṃ cana; priyābhirāmaṃ vicarantam antarā
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus that youth, who resembled the foremost of Gandharvas, was honored by the delighted king Virata. And no others knew him in the least as he moved about among them, charming and agreeable.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi matsye nyavasanta pāṇḍavā; yathāpratijñābhir amoghadarśanāḥ ajñātacaryāṃ vyacaran samāhitāḥ; samudranemīpatayo 'tiduḥkhitāḥ
english: Thus the Pandavas, those lords whose vision never fails and whose vows are unfailing, dwelt in the land of Matsya, passing their time of incognito with composed minds — they who are lords whose realm extends to the rim of the ocean — in great suffering.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ matsyasya nagare vasantas tatra pāṇḍavāḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ mahāvīryāḥ kim akurvanta vai dvija
english: Janamejaya said: 'When the Pandavas of great valor were dwelling thus in the city of Matsya, O brahmin, what did they do after that?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ te nyavasaṃs tatra pracchannāḥ kurunandanāḥ ārādhayanto rājānaṃ yad akurvanta tac chṛṇu
english: Vaishampayana said: 'Hear what those descendants of Kuru, concealed in that place, did while dwelling there and pleasing the king.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sabhāstāraḥ sabhyānām abhavat priyaḥ tathaiva ca virāṭasya saputrasya viśāṃ pate
english: Yudhishthira became the beloved companion of the assembly members in the hall, and likewise a favorite of Virata and his son, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: sa hy akṣahṛdayajñas tān krīḍayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ akṣavatyāṃ yathākāmaṃ sūtrabaddhān iva dvijān
english: For that Pandava, knowing the secrets of dice, entertained them at gambling as he pleased, like a puppeteer controlling brahmins on strings.

sanskrit: ajñātaṃ ca virāṭasya vijitya vasu dharmarāṭ bhrātṛbhyaḥ puruṣavyāghro yathārhaṃ sma prayacchati
english: And the king of righteousness, that tiger among men, secretly winning Virata's wealth, would distribute it fittingly among his brothers.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi māṃsāni bhakṣyāni vividhāni ca atisṛṣṭāni matsyena vikrīṇāti yudhiṣṭhire
english: Bhimasena too, with the various eatables and meats lavishly provided by Matsya, would sell them and give the proceeds to Yudhishthira.

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi parijīrṇāni labdhāny antaḥpure 'rjunaḥ vikrīṇānaś ca sarvebhyaḥ pāṇḍavebhyaḥ prayacchati
english: Arjuna too, obtaining worn-out garments from the women's quarters, would sell them and distribute the proceeds to all the Pandavas.

sanskrit: sahadevo 'pi gopānāṃ veṣam āsthāya pāṇḍavaḥ dadhi kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ caiva pāṇḍavebhyaḥ prayacchati
english: Sahadeva too, that Pandava, adopting the guise of a cowherd, would provide curds, milk, and ghee to the Pandavas.

sanskrit: nakulo 'pi dhanaṃ labdhvā kṛte karmaṇi vājinām tuṣṭe tasmin narapatau pāṇḍavebhyaḥ prayacchati
english: Nakula too, obtaining wealth for his work with the horses when that lord of men was pleased, would give it to the Pandavas.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāpi sarvān bhrātṝṃs tān nirīkṣantī tapasvinī yathā punar avijñātā tathā carati bhāminī
english: And Krishna too — that noble lady in her suffering — would look upon all those brothers and move about as before, unrecognized.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃpādayantas te tathānyonyaṃ mahārathāḥ prekṣamāṇās tadā kṛṣṇām ūṣuś channā narādhipa
english: Thus those great warriors, providing for each other in this way, and yet beholding Krishna in that condition, dwelt there in concealment, O lord of men.

sanskrit: atha māse caturthe tu brahmaṇaḥ sumahotsavaḥ āsīt samṛddho matsyeṣu puruṣāṇāṃ susaṃmataḥ
english: Then, in the fourth month, there arose a grand festival of Brahma among the Matsyas — prosperous and well-regarded by the people.

sanskrit: tatra mallāḥ samāpetur digbhyo rājan sahasraśaḥ mahākāyā mahāvīryāḥ kālakhañjā ivāsurāḥ
english: There, wrestlers gathered from all directions, O king, by the thousands — of great bodies and great strength, like the Kalakhanja demons.

sanskrit: vīryonnaddhā balodagrā rājñā samabhipūjitāḥ siṃhaskandhakaṭigrīvāḥ svavadātā manasvinaḥ asakṛllabdhalakṣās te raṅge pārthivasaṃnidhau
english: Swelling with valor, overflowing with strength, honored by the king, with shoulders, waists, and necks like lions — proud and high-minded men who had repeatedly won glory in the arena before the king.

sanskrit: teṣām eko mahān āsīt sarvamallān samāhvayat āvalgamānaṃ taṃ raṅge nopatiṣṭhati kaś cana
english: Among them one was pre-eminent and challenged all the wrestlers. As he strutted about the arena, none would stand up to him.

sanskrit: yadā sarve vimanasas te mallā hatacetasaḥ atha sūdena taṃ mallaṃ yodhayām āsa matsyarāṭ
english: When all the wrestlers were disheartened and their spirits broken, the king of Matsya had that wrestler fight against his cook.

sanskrit: codyamānas tato bhīmo duḥkhenaivākaron matim na hi śaknoti vivṛte pratyākhyātuṃ narādhipam
english: Then Bhima, though urged with difficulty, made up his mind — for in public he could not refuse the lord of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghraḥ śārdūlaśithilaṃ caran praviveśa mahāraṅgaṃ virāṭam abhiharṣayan
english: Then that tiger among men, moving with the relaxed gait of a lion, entered the great arena, filling Virata with delight.

sanskrit: babandha kakṣyāṃ kaunteyas tatas taṃ harṣayañ janam tatas taṃ vṛtrasaṃkāśaṃ bhīmo mallaṃ samāhvayat
english: The son of Kunti tied his sash and thereupon gladdened the crowd. Then Bhima challenged that wrestler who was like Vritra himself.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau sumahotsāhāv ubhau tīvraparākramau mattāv iva mahākāyau vāraṇau ṣaṣṭihāyanau
english: Both were of tremendous enthusiasm and both of fierce valor — like two great bull elephants of sixty years in rut.

sanskrit: cakarṣa dorbhyām utpāṭya bhīmo mallam amitrahā vinadantam abhikrośañ śārdūla iva vāraṇam
english: Bhima, slayer of enemies, tearing the wrestler away with his arms, dragged him — roaring and shrieking — like a tiger with an elephant.

sanskrit: tam udyamya mahābāhur bhrāmayām āsa vīryavān tato mallāś ca matsyāś ca vismayaṃ cakrire param
english: The mighty-armed and valorous one, lifting him up, whirled him around. Then both the wrestlers and the Matsyas were struck with the greatest amazement.

sanskrit: bhrāmayitvā śataguṇaṃ gatasattvam acetanam pratyapiṃṣan mahābāhur mallaṃ bhuvi vṛkodaraḥ
english: Having whirled him a hundredfold, with the wrestler's life gone and his senses extinguished, the mighty-armed Vrikodara ground him into the earth.

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate malle jīmūte lokaviśrute virāṭaḥ paramaṃ harṣam agacchad bāndhavaiḥ saha
english: When that wrestler Jimuta, world-renowned, was slain, Virata was filled with the utmost joy along with his kinsmen.

sanskrit: saṃharṣāt pradadau vittaṃ bahu rājā mahāmanāḥ ballavāya mahāraṅge yathā vaiśravaṇas tathā
english: Overflowing with joy, the high-minded king gave great wealth to Ballava in the great arena, as generously as Kubera himself.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa subahūn mallān puruṣāṃś ca mahābalān vinighnan matsyarājasya prītim āvahad uttamām
english: In this way, slaying very many wrestlers and men of great strength, he brought the highest delight to the king of Matsya.

sanskrit: yadāsya tulyaḥ puruṣo na kaś cit tatra vidyate tato vyāghraiś ca siṃhaiś ca dviradaiś cāpy ayodhayat
english: When no man equal to him could be found there, he then fought with tigers and lions and elephants as well.

sanskrit: punar antaḥpuragataḥ strīṇāṃ madhye vṛkodaraḥ yodhyate sma virāṭena siṃhair mattair mahābalaiḥ
english: Again, having entered the women's quarters, Vrikodara would fight among the women at Virata's command against maddened lions of great strength.

sanskrit: bībhatsur api gītena sunṛttena ca pāṇḍavaḥ virāṭaṃ toṣayām āsa sarvāś cāntaḥpurastriyaḥ
english: And Bibhatsu too, that Pandava, satisfied Virata and all the women of the inner quarters with song and beautiful dancing.

sanskrit: aśvair vinītair javanais tatra tatra samāgataiḥ toṣayām āsa nakulo rājānaṃ rājasattama
english: With well-trained and swift horses gathered from various places, Nakula gratified the king, O best of kings.

sanskrit: tasmai pradeyaṃ prāyacchat prīto rājā dhanaṃ bahu vinītān vṛṣabhān dṛṣṭvā sahadevasya cābhibho
english: Pleased upon seeing the well-trained cattle belonging to Sahadeva, the king gave him much wealth as his due reward, O mighty one.

sanskrit: evaṃ te nyavasaṃs tatra pracchannāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ karmāṇi tasya kurvāṇā virāṭanṛpates tadā
english: Thus those bulls among men lived there in concealment, performing services for Virata the king in those days.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vasamāneṣu pārtheṣu matsyasya nagare tadā mahāratheṣu channeṣu māsā daśa samatyayuḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: While the sons of Pritha, those great warriors, were dwelling thus in concealment in the city of Matsya, ten months passed by.

sanskrit: yājñasenī sudeṣṇāṃ tu śuśrūṣantī viśāṃ pate avasat paricārārhā suduḥkhaṃ janamejaya
english: Yajnaseni, serving Sudeshna, O lord of the people, dwelt there in great suffering — she who deserved to be served, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: tathā carantīṃ pāñcālīṃ sudeṣṇāyā niveśane senāpatir virāṭasya dadarśa jalajānanām
english: As she moved about in that manner in Sudeshna's household, the commander of Virata's army beheld the Pancali, she of lotus-like face.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā devagarbhābhāṃ carantīṃ devatām iva kīcakaḥ kāmayām āsa kāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ
english: Seeing her as she moved about, radiant as one born of divine seed, like a goddess herself, Kichaka desired her, pierced by the arrows of Kama.

sanskrit: sa tu kāmāgnisaṃtaptaḥ sudeṣṇām abhigamya vai prahasann iva senānīr idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Scorched by the fire of desire, the commander approached Sudeshna and, as if smiling, spoke these words:

sanskrit: neyaṃ purā jātu mayeha dṛṣṭā; rājño virāṭasya niveśane śubhā rūpeṇa conmādayatīva māṃ bhṛśaṃ; gandhena jātā madireva bhāminī
english: 'This beautiful one was never seen by me before in the abode of King Virata. With her beauty she maddens me utterly — this lady, born fragrant like wine.'

sanskrit: kā devarūpā hṛdayaṃgamā śubhe; ācakṣva me kā ca kutaś ca śobhanā cittaṃ hi nirmathya karoti māṃ vaśe; na cānyad atrauṣadham adya me matam
english: 'Who is this one with the form of a goddess, captivating to the heart, O fair one? Tell me — who is she and where is she from, this lovely woman? She churns my mind and brings me under her sway. I know no other remedy for this today.'

sanskrit: aho taveyaṃ paricārikā śubhā; pratyagrarūpā pratibhāti mām iyam ayuktarūpaṃ hi karoti karma te; praśāstu māṃ yac ca mamāsti kiṃ cana
english: 'Ah, this handmaid of yours is beautiful — she of fresh, youthful beauty appears before me. Indeed she performs work unworthy of her form. Let her command me and all that I possess.'

sanskrit: prabhūtanāgāśvarathaṃ mahādhanaṃ; samṛddhiyuktaṃ bahupānabhojanam manoharaṃ kāñcanacitrabhūṣaṇaṃ; gṛhaṃ mahac chobhayatām iyaṃ mama
english: 'Let her adorn my great house — rich in elephants, horses, and chariots, possessed of great wealth, full of prosperity, with abundant drink and food, charming, decorated with golden ornaments.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sudeṣṇām anumantrya kīcakas; tataḥ samabhyetya narādhipātmajām uvāca kṛṣṇām abhisāntvayaṃs tadā; mṛgendrakanyām iva jambuko vane
english: Then Kichaka, having taken leave of Sudeshna, approached the daughter of the king of men and spoke then to Krishna with words of enticement — like a jackal in the forest approaching the daughter of the lion.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca rūpaṃ prathamaṃ ca te vayo; nirarthakaṃ kevalam adya bhāmini adhāryamāṇā srag ivottamā yathā; na śobhase sundari śobhanā satī
english: 'This beauty of yours, and your youth — both are rendered purposeless and barren today, O passionate one. Like a supreme garland that goes unworn, you do not shine, O beautiful one, though you are truly lovely.'

sanskrit: tyajāmi dārān mama ye purātanā; bhavantu dāsyas tava cāruhāsini ahaṃ ca te sundari dāsavat sthitaḥ; sadā bhaviṣye vaśago varānane
english: 'I will abandon my former wives — let them become your maidservants, O fair-smiling one. And I myself, O beautiful woman, shall stand like a slave before you; I shall always be under your command, O lovely-faced one.'

sanskrit: draupady uvāca aprārthanīyām iha māṃ sūtaputrābhimanyase vihīnavarṇāṃ sairandhrīṃ bībhatsāṃ keśakārikām
english: Draupadi said: 'O son of a charioteer, you court me here as one not to be courted — a Sairandhri woman of lower standing, a contemptible hairdresser.'

sanskrit: paradārāsmi bhadraṃ te na yuktaṃ tvayi sāṃpratam dayitāḥ prāṇināṃ dārā dharmaṃ samanucintaya
english: 'I am another's wife — may it be well with you; this is not fitting for you at this time. The wives of living beings are dear to them — reflect on dharma.'

sanskrit: paradāre na te buddhir jātu kāryā kathaṃ cana vivarjanaṃ hy akāryāṇām etat satpuruṣavratam
english: 'Your mind should never in any way turn toward another's wife. The renunciation of improper deeds — that is the vow of good men.'

sanskrit: mithyābhigṛdhno hi naraḥ pāpātmā moham āsthitaḥ ayaśaḥ prāpnuyād ghoraṃ sumahat prāpnuyād bhayam
english: 'For a man of sinful soul who wrongly lusts and has entered into delusion will gain terrible infamy and will incur very great fear.'

sanskrit: mā sūtaputra hṛṣyasva mādya tyakṣyasi jīvitam durlabhām abhimanvāno māṃ vīrair abhirakṣitām
english: 'Do not be elated, O son of a charioteer — today you will lose your life, coveting me who am difficult to attain, guarded by heroes.'

sanskrit: na cāpy ahaṃ tvayā śakyā gandharvāḥ patayo mama te tvāṃ nihanyuḥ kupitāḥ sādhv alaṃ mā vyanīnaśaḥ
english: 'And I cannot be taken by you. My husbands are Gandharvas — they will kill you when angered. Stop, it is enough — do not bring about your own destruction.'

sanskrit: aśakyarūpaiḥ puruṣair adhvānaṃ gantum icchasi yathā niścetano bālaḥ kūlasthaḥ kūlam uttaram tartum icchati mandātmā tathā tvaṃ kartum icchasi
english: 'Just as a foolish boy, standing on a bank, mindlessly wishes to cross to the far bank though he cannot — so you, a man who cannot accomplish what you desire, wish to do what is beyond you.'

sanskrit: antarmahīṃ vā yadi vordhvam utpateḥ; samudrapāraṃ yadi vā pradhāvasi tathāpi teṣāṃ na vimokṣam arhasi; pramāthino devasutā hi me varāḥ
english: 'Whether you enter the earth, or fly upward, or run to the far shore of the ocean — even so you shall not escape them. For my husbands are mighty sons of gods.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ kālarātrīm iva kaś cid āturaḥ; kiṃ māṃ dṛḍhaṃ prārthayase 'dya kīcaka kiṃ mātur aṅke śayito yathā śiśuś; candraṃ jighṛkṣur iva manyase hi mām
english: 'Like some afflicted man who rushes toward the night of doom — why do you importune me so stubbornly today, O Kichaka? Do you think of me like a child lying in its mother's lap who wants to grasp the moon?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pratyākhyāto rājaputryā sudeṣṇāṃ kīcako 'bravīt amaryādena kāmena ghoreṇābhipariplutaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Rejected by the princess-born, Kichaka, overwhelmed by unbridled and terrible desire, spoke to Sudeshna:

sanskrit: yathā kaikeyi sairandhryā sameyāṃ tad vidhīyatām tāṃ sudeṣṇe parīpsasva māhaṃ prāṇān prahāsiṣam
english: 'Let it be arranged that I may meet with the Sairandhri by some means, O Kaikeyi. Seek to obtain her for me, Sudeshna — otherwise I shall give up my life.'

sanskrit: tasya tāṃ bahuśaḥ śrutvā vācaṃ vilapatas tadā virāṭamahiṣī devī kṛpāṃ cakre manasvinī
english: Hearing his lamentations again and again, the wise queen, chief consort of Virata, felt compassion for him.

sanskrit: svam artham abhisaṃdhāya tasyārtham anucintya ca udvegaṃ caiva kṛṣṇāyāḥ sudeṣṇā sūtam abravīt
english: Keeping her own interest in mind and reflecting upon his interest as well, and also upon Krishna's distress, Sudeshna spoke to the charioteer's son:

sanskrit: parviṇīṃ tvaṃ samuddiṣya surām annaṃ ca kāraya tatraināṃ preṣayiṣyāmi surāhārīṃ tavāntikam
english: 'You prepare wine and food on the occasion of the festival day. I will send her to you there — the wine-fetcher — into your presence.'

sanskrit: tatra saṃpreṣitām enāṃ vijane niravagrahām sāntvayethā yathākāmaṃ sāntvyamānā ramed yadi
english: 'There, when she has been sent and is alone without restraint, you may coax her as you please — if, when coaxed, she is willing to sport with you.'

sanskrit: kīcakas tu gṛhaṃ gatvā bhaginyā vacanāt tadā surām āhārayām āsa rājārhāṃ suparisrutām
english: Kichaka then, going home at his sister's word, had wine fetched — of royal quality, well-filtered and refined.

sanskrit: ājaurabhraṃ ca subhṛśaṃ bahūṃś coccāvacān mṛgān kārayām āsa kuśalair annapānaṃ suśobhanam
english: And he had much roast meat and many kinds of game, great and small, prepared by skilled cooks — splendid food and drink.

sanskrit: tasmin kṛte tadā devī kīcakenopamantritā sudeṣṇā preṣayām āsa sairandhrīṃ kīcakālayam
english: When this had been done and Kichaka had sent word to the queen, Sudeshna dispatched the Sairandhri to Kichaka's dwelling.

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca uttiṣṭha gaccha sairandhri kīcakasya niveśanam pānam ānaya kalyāṇi pipāsā māṃ prabādhate
english: Sudeshna said: 'Rise and go, Sairandhri, to Kichaka's dwelling. Bring wine, dear one — thirst torments me.'

sanskrit: draupady uvāca na gaccheyam ahaṃ tasya rājaputri niveśanam tvam eva rājñi jānāsi yathā sa nirapatrapaḥ
english: Draupadi said: 'I should not go to his dwelling, O princess. You yourself know, O queen, how shameless he is.'

sanskrit: na cāham anavadyāṅgi tava veśmani bhāmini kāmavṛttā bhaviṣyāmi patīnāṃ vyabhicāriṇī
english: 'And I, O blameless-limbed one, O passionate lady, shall not become one who acts out of lust in your house, unfaithful to my husbands.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ caiva devi jānāsi yathā sa samayaḥ kṛtaḥ praviśantyā mayā pūrvaṃ tava veśmani bhāmini
english: 'And you yourself know, O goddess, what agreement was made when I first entered your house, O passionate one.'

sanskrit: kīcakaś ca sukeśānte mūḍho madanadarpitaḥ so 'vamaṃsyati māṃ dṛṣṭvā na yāsye tatra śobhane
english: 'And Kichaka — foolish and arrogant with the pride of Kama — he will dishonor me upon seeing me. I will not go there, O lovely one.'

sanskrit: santi bahvyas tava preṣyā rājaputri vaśānugāḥ anyāṃ preṣaya bhadraṃ te sa hi mām avamaṃsyate
english: 'You have many other attendants obedient to your command, O princess — send another. May it be well with you, for he will dishonor me.'

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca naiva tvāṃ jātu hiṃsyāt sa itaḥ saṃpreṣitāṃ mayā
english: Sudeshna said: 'He will never harm you when you are sent by me from here.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity asyāḥ pradadau kāṃsyaṃ sapidhānaṃ hiraṇmayam sā śaṅkamānā rudatī daivaṃ śaraṇam īyuṣī prātiṣṭhata surāhārī kīcakasya niveśanam
english: Vaishampayana said: With these words she placed in her hands a bronze vessel with a golden lid. She, full of suspicion, weeping, having taken refuge in fate, set forth as the wine-fetcher to Kichaka's dwelling.
